objective_for_doctor: A 5-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a fever, does the person have a whooping cough, and significant dyspnea.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Hi doctor. I have a fever and I’m having a lot of trouble breathing. I also make more saliva than usual, and I have a harsh breathing sound (stridor).

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given your fever, severe trouble breathing, extra saliva, and stridor, I’m concerned about an upper-airway obstruction or a serious throat infection; can you tell me: when did the symptoms start, and is your breathing worse when you’re lying down?  
Patient:
My symptoms started today (earlier this morning). My breathing feels worse when I lie down, so I’ve been trying to stay more upright.

Doctor: I’m going to ask a focused question to narrow this down: do you have a barking cough, trouble swallowing/drooling, or a muffled “hot potato” voice?  
Patient:
Yes, I have a barking cough. I’m drooling more than usual, and my voice sounds a bit muffled.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—your barking cough, drooling, muffled voice, and stridor with fever strongly suggest an acute upper-airway infection; can you tell me if you can swallow fluids at all, and whether you see your neck pulling in (retractions) or if he is unusually sleepy or worsening quickly?  
Patient:
I can swallow some fluids, but it’s hard. I think his neck is pulling in when he breathes, and he seems like he’s getting worse pretty quickly.

Doctor: This sounds like a potentially life-threatening airway infection (likely croup, epiglottitis, or retropharyngeal involvement); can you tell me your temperature and whether he’s had any recent choking/foreign body or a sore throat before today?  
Doctor: Also, right now, is he able to talk/cry normally, and are you hearing harsh stridor even at rest (not only when upset)?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry (SpO2) and REQUEST TEST: Lateral_Neck_and_or_Chest_XRay to assess for epiglottitis/airway narrowing.

I don’t know his exact temperature, but he does have a fever. No recent choking/foreign body, and no sore throat before today.

Right now he can’t really talk—he’s more quiet/crying weakly—and the harsh stridor is there even when he’s resting, not only when he’s upset.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—based on drooling, muffled voice, stridor at rest, inability to talk/cry normally, and rapid worsening, I’m most concerned about **acute epiglottitis** rather than typical viral croup; can you confirm if he looks very ill/toxic and whether he’s sitting upright with neck extended (tripod posture)?  
Patient:  

Doctor: I’m going to decide now—**DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute epiglottitis (life-threatening upper airway infection)**
